```{r}
#| label: setup

# Quarto renders with the working directory set to this document's folder
# (dev/), so golem::pkg_path() would resolve relative paths against dev/ and
# miss the database the app writes at the project root. Anchor everything to
# the package root by walking up to the first directory with a DESCRIPTION.
find_pkg_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  path <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"))) {
      return(path)
    }
    parent <- dirname(path)
    if (identical(parent, path)) {
      stop("Could not find package root (no DESCRIPTION above ", start, ").")
    }
    path <- parent
  }
}
pkg_root <- find_pkg_root()

# Choose the config. QUIZ_REPORT_CONFIG is checked first and is specific to
# this report: the project .Renviron pins GOLEM_CONFIG_ACTIVE="default" and is
# loaded at R startup, which would otherwise override a value passed on the
# command line. Use a dedicated variable that nothing in .Renviron sets, e.g.
#   QUIZ_REPORT_CONFIG=production quarto preview dev/leaderboard_report.qmd
# Falls back to GOLEM_CONFIG_ACTIVE, then R_CONFIG_ACTIVE, then "default".
config <- Sys.getenv(
  "QUIZ_REPORT_CONFIG",
  Sys.getenv("GOLEM_CONFIG_ACTIVE", Sys.getenv("R_CONFIG_ACTIVE", "default"))
)

# Quarto previews/renders run R from dev/, so the project root .Renviron (with
# the PG_* / AWS_* secrets) may not be loaded. Load it here so the Postgres
# (production) config can connect. It must not override the config chosen
# above, so restore that afterward.
renviron_path <- file.path(pkg_root, ".Renviron")
if (file.exists(renviron_path)) {
  readRenviron(renviron_path)
  Sys.setenv(GOLEM_CONFIG_ACTIVE = config)
}

pkgload::load_all(pkg_root, quiet = TRUE)

library(DBI)
library(gt)
db_backend <- get_golem_config("db_backend", config = config)

# Connect to the same database the app uses for this config. Use a single
# DBI connection (no pool) since this is a one-shot render.
if (identical(db_backend, "sqlite")) {
  sqlite_path <- file.path(
    pkg_root,
    get_golem_config("sqlite_path", config = config)
  )
  db <- db_connect("sqlite", sqlite_path = sqlite_path, use_pool = FALSE)
  source_label <- paste0("SQLite (", sqlite_path, ")")
} else if (identical(db_backend, "postgres")) {
  db <- db_connect("postgres", use_pool = FALSE)
  source_label <- paste0("Postgres database '", Sys.getenv("PG_DATABASE"), "'")
} else {
  stop("Unsupported db_backend: ", db_backend, call. = FALSE)
}
# Close the connection when the document finishes rendering.
db_create_tables(db)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Data source"}
Config **`r config`** &middot; `r source_label` &middot; generated
`r format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")`
:::

```{r}
#| label: leaderboard

# Show every submitted attempt, ranked the same way the app ranks them.
board <- db_leaderboard(db, n = .Machine$integer.max)
db_close(db)
```

```{r}
#| label: render-leaderboard

if (nrow(board) == 0) {
  cat("No submitted attempts yet.")
} else {
  player <- ifelse(
    is.na(board$name) | !nzchar(board$name),
    board$user_id,
    board$name
  )
  # Stored names are often email addresses; show only the local part (before
  # the @). Values without an @ (e.g. a user_id fallback) are left unchanged.
  player <- sub("@.*$", "", player)

  display <- data.frame(
    rank = seq_len(nrow(board)),
    player = player,
    score = paste0(board$score, " / ", board$n_questions),
    percent = board$score / board$n_questions,
    time = sprintf(
      "%d:%02d",
      board$duration_seconds %/% 60,
      round(board$duration_seconds %% 60)
    )
  )

  gt(display) |>
    cols_label(
      rank = "Rank",
      player = "Player",
      score = "Score",
      percent = "Percent",
      time = "Time"
    ) |>
    fmt_percent(columns = percent, decimals = 0) |>
    cols_align(align = "right", columns = c(rank, score, percent, time)) |>
    cols_align(align = "left", columns = player) |>
    # Medal colors for the top three places.
    data_color(
      columns = rank,
      rows = rank <= 3,
      target_columns = everything(),
      palette = c("#f7d94c", "#d7d7d7", "#e0a46b"),
      domain = c(1, 3),
      reverse = TRUE
    ) |>
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(22),
      column_labels.font.size = px(18),
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      data_row.padding = px(10),
      table.width = pct(100)
    ) |>
    opt_row_striping()
}
```
